name: Quasi
label: Touch and Go
lede: Sam Coomes and Janet Weiss were married for four years and have been a band for more than thirty: one man on a rocksichord, one woman on drums, and a sound bigger than two people should make.

eras.title: Motorgoat, then two
eras.text: Sam Coomes came up from San Francisco's The Donner Party; Janet Weiss had taught herself drums by watching other drummers and moved to Portland in 1989. Their first band together had three people in it. The one that lasted had two.

years.h: Coomes, Weiss and Brad Pedinov form Motorgoat
years.p: The Portland trio puts out two self-released cassettes and one 7-inch before folding in 1993.

years.h: Quasi starts as a duo in Portland
years.p: Coomes and Weiss record as a two-piece, self-release a cassette and a CD, and try out extra players live before deciding two is enough on stage too.
years.xp: Coomes plays guitar, bass and keyboards, a Rocksichord among them, and both of them sing. Weiss told Spin the marriage lasted four years; the band outlived it by decades.

years.h: Weiss joins Sleater-Kinney
years.p: Weiss becomes [[Sleater-Kinney|e36e78eb-3ace-4acd-882c-16789e700ab7]]'s fourth drummer after seeing Corin Tucker and Carrie Brownstein play. Quasi stays her other full-time band. Key Op puts out Quasi's Early Recordings.

eras.title: Opening for Elliott Smith, then backing him
eras.text: Signed to Seattle's Up Records, Quasi made three albums in three years in Portland basements and studios. Coomes's old Heatmiser bandmate Elliott Smith took them on tour as his opener, and then as his band.

years.h: R&B Transmogrification, cut in Pond's basement
years.p: Quasi's first record for Up is made in the basement studio of Portland band Pond.

years.h: Featuring "Birds" makes the Pazz & Jop poll
years.p: Recorded at Jackpot! in November 1997 with Larry Crane. Pitchfork gives it 8.6, and the Village Voice critics' poll puts it at No. 25 for the year.
years.xp: Rolling Stone's Sean Kennerly heard heartache and despair hidden "inside sugary vocal harmonies and catchy, succinct songwriting." Several songs were left over from the R&B Transmogrification sessions.

years.src: Variety · Wikipedia: Quasi · Wikipedia: Sam Coomes
years.h: Elliott Smith plays bass in Quasi's set at the Roxy
years.p: On Smith's XO tour, Smith joins the opening duo on bass mid-set, then Coomes and Weiss back him for the headline show. Two nights at the Roxy in Los Angeles, 450 capacity, $10.
years.xp:
Variety's Troy J. Augusto wasn't sold on the double act, writing that the shows felt like two sets by the same band. He also noted Quasi had been touring with Smith on and off for about two years.

The tours ran through 1998 and 1999 across the US, Europe, Australia and Japan. Coomes also played bass and sang on several of Smith's records.

yt: Live at the Echo Lounge, Atlanta, October 1999
years.h: Field Studies closes out the Up years
years.p: The third Up album, made with producer [[Phil Ek|974863b2-1c82-4bb7-b23f-54ddf2713e88]]. Domino handles it in Europe, as it would every Quasi album through 2013.

eras.title: Home recordings on Touch and Go
eras.text: The move to Touch and Go came with a turn inward: the first album for the label was recorded at home, the second in a pair of Portland rooms, and only the third went to an outside producer.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Sword of God · Wikipedia: Quasi
years.h: The Sword of God is made at home and sounds like a bar band
years.p: Recorded at Fluke Room and the Devil's Workshop in Portland. Billboard calls it "mangier, almost bar-band." Touch and Go also reissues Early Recordings.
years.xp: Reviews split. AllMusic's Thom Jurek singled out Weiss, writing that she'd become "a stomping drummer." Pitchfork thought the reach for a wider range fell flat. Stanley Zappa plays saxophone on one track.

years.h: Hot Shit! comes with a free live record
years.p: Early copies and the Domino edition add Live Shit, 19 live tracks. Pitchfork gives the album 5.2; Metacritic's average is 78.

years.src: Wikipedia: When the Going Gets Dark
years.h: Dave Fridmann produces When the Going Gets Dark
years.p: The Flaming Lips and [[Mercury Rev|7b1cf87e-c54f-4abc-893d-90245a31900d]] producer mixes the duo for its third Touch and Go album, released with Domino in Europe.

years.cap: Joanna Bolme and Janet Weiss, Green Man festival, 2006
years.h: Joanna Bolme joins on bass for the tour
years.p: [[Joanna Bolme|21f4bc79-8b24-4aee-85b3-22f46cf2e5d2]], who plays with Weiss in [[Stephen Malkmus and the Jicks|98e4bf9e-9e33-4f07-9962-f7c1c2d773ba]], tours with Quasi through 2006.

eras.title: Three, then two again
eras.text: For four years Quasi was a trio. The band toured with labelmates, left Touch and Go for Kill Rock Stars, and then went back to the shape it started in.

years.cap: Quasi at Rickshaw Stop, San Francisco
years.h: Bolme becomes a full member, and they tour with Ted Leo
years.p: Just before a US tour with Touch and Go labelmates [[Ted Leo and the Pharmacists|31095622-5a1e-4f22-8ad1-b08eb6255f37]], the band tells CMJ that Bolme is in for good.

years.h: American Gong, the trio's only album
years.p: The first Quasi record for Kill Rock Stars, with Bolme on bass. The deluxe edition adds So Far So Good, a two-CD anthology.

years.cap: Quasi opening for Sebadoh at the Rickshaw Theatre, Vancouver, February 2011
years.h: Back to a two-piece "for the foreseeable future"
years.p: Quasi thanks Bolme on Facebook and returns to the original duo line-up.

years.h: Mole City, then a covers EP with 'War Pigs' on it
years.p: The duo's Kill Rock Stars follow-up. A covers EP, Interprets, takes on Queen, Black Sabbath, Marvin Gaye and Nick Lowe.

eras.title: The crash and the comeback
eras.text: Weiss left Sleater-Kinney in the summer of 2019, and weeks later a car accident took her off the drums. While she recovered, Coomes kept bringing new songs to their practice space, and those songs became an album.

years.h: A car crash breaks Weiss's leg and collarbone, and Quasi cancels
years.p: Six weeks after leaving Sleater-Kinney, Weiss breaks her right leg and left collarbone, and Quasi's newly announced tour is called off.
years.xp: Weiss said she was "so happy to be alive." She couldn't walk for almost three months, she told Off Shelf, and it took another two years to get her strength and coordination back. Her sister started a GoFundMe for the medical bills.

years.h: 'Last Days of the Thin Blue Line Lie' goes up on Bandcamp
years.p: A one-off single written around the George Floyd protests, with proceeds going to the nonprofit Don't Shoot Portland.

q: We treated the recording process like a live show, almost.
years.src: Post-Trash · Spin · Off Shelf · Wikipedia: Breaking the Balls of History
years.h: Breaking the Balls of History, five days at Robert Lang
years.p: Their tenth album, made with John Goodmanson at Robert Lang Studios in Shoreline, Washington, and paid for before any label heard it. Sub Pop, Weiss's old Sleater-Kinney label, takes it.
years.xp:
"We treated the recording process like a live show, almost," Coomes told Post-Trash. Weiss said the live energy you hear is intentional.

Metacritic's average is 82. Uncut called Weiss "perhaps the greatest rock drummer alive"; Pitchfork, at 6.3, was cooler.

yt: Quasi, full performance live on KEXP, 2023
years.h: Thirty years in, a full set on KEXP
years.p: The duo plays the new songs live in the Seattle station's studio.

years.h: Featuring "Birds", played start to finish
years.p: Quasi tours as a three-piece again, playing the 1998 album in full.
